findings.title: B1 is not fully fixed: when a value is changed to '' after a fill, the script exits 0 and the old text stays in the policy (the stated limit says HOSTING_REGIONS is covered, but it is not)
findings.evidence: probe_refill.py on temp copies in the notes folder (none in the worktree): a full fill (rc0), then one change, then a --dry-run. HOSTING_REGIONS 'Ireland' -> '' (and _AR -> ''): rc0, no output; the policy still says ', and in Ireland (our database, hosting and temporary-storage providers)'. The fill-in data comment documents '' as a legitimate value ('' when unknown). PRIVACY_EMAIL -> '': rc0, the old email stays, although a first fill refuses '' ('is empty but the documents use it'). Cause: scripts/fill_in_legal.py clause_problems() skips every {value} table (the 'any("{value}" in str(t) ...)' line, file line 294), and _unapplied_values() skips empty values ('not value.strip()', line 354). The fix report's stated limit says 'HOSTING_REGIONS_CLAUSE ... caught through ... the HOSTING_REGIONS placeholder check'. That holds only when one non-empty value is changed to another. The realistic B1 path is fixed: a native-review change to WITHDRAW_PATH_AR or GOVERNING_LAW_AR that is not a substring of the old value exits 3 (6 parametrized nodes plus my probes: ANON_LOG_RETENTION rc3, deletion 043->old rc3; a territories re-select rc0 writes correctly; the same data rc0 with no change).
findings.fix: In clause_problems, when a {value} table's selected key is 'empty', require the literal tail of the 'nonempty' variant (variant.split('{value}', 1)[1], e.g. ' (our database, hosting and temporary-storage providers)') to be absent from that language's documents. In _unapplied_values, refuse '' for every key except HOSTING_REGIONS / HOSTING_REGIONS_AR, which matches what a first fill already enforces. Append one parametrized case (HOSTING_REGIONS -> '') to the B1 nodes, and correct the stated limit.
